origin_bridge_interpretation: Adapter samples centerline ahead of projected progress, but Controller prepends ego origin as t=0. First target segment therefore includes lateral/longitudinal gap to the route, not only .25s cruise displacement.

At3514 all three presets start firstpoint[3.474663,3.376833]m ->19.380933m/s, while first future-to-future segment is8m/s. Initial true cross-track is3.145584m and pose error.412188m, so offset is mainly parking-start geometry rather than localization noise.
Both diagnostic target and reference read the same timed arc and share this bridge error; agreement between them cannot prove tracking configured8m/s.

At5Hz replanning source age remains below.2s, within the first.25s artificial segment: reference_speed keeps reading its slope while near target blends it with the next segment. This is a route-adapter timing/geometry limitation, not a proven actual speed19.38m/s.
At rest both8m/s and19.38m/s requests saturate throttle.75; numeric target excess alone does not prove a different first actuator command or explain a collision.
limits: Only finalized available attempts are analyzed. Pending/missing groups are not treated as successes.
Collision message coordinates in pinned atomic_criteria.py are ego actor positions, not obstacle centers.
No obstacle polygons, peer actor trajectories or contact force time series were logged; exact obstruction geometry and release mechanism cannot be proved.
Logged truth cross-track is evaluated relative to the diagnostic route with an estimator-progress search bound; large branch errors may limit interpretation.
Origin-to-firstpoint bridge affects both target_speed and reference_speed diagnostics; their agreement is not an independent cruise-speed validation.
No frozen implementation or official outcomes are changed by this analysis.
